So, I'm 14 11/12, and I went to my Grandmother's a little while ago. Naturally, her (Windows Vista) computer had some trouble. I ask her what happens (paraphrasing; can't quite remember):

Me: So, what happens?

Grandma: Well, when I turn it off for the night and go to bed, in the morning it doesn't come on all the way.

... one figuring out what she means later ...

Me: So, what you're saying is that after it starts up, it gets to the desktop and freezes?

Grandma: Yes.

I check if it's defaulting to hibernation or suspend-to-RAM, it's not. Puzzler. I spend a while power-cycling it to see if it freezes so I can see exactly what's happening. It doesn't. A few hours of looking in the registry for virus traces or corruption later,

Grandma: Oh... The Windows update thing wants to run?

Me: Oh, yeah. Let's do that; it might fix it.

I launch Windows Update, and it's a SERVICE PACK. Yes, a Vista installation that still doesn't have all the service packs. sigh. I run the install, and we leave to do some other stuff. When we get back, the install's failed. I try again, and it fails the install, starts backing out to the ReMangle point, and hangs. GREAT. I reset the machine, and it restarts the back-out, and hangs again. This goes a few times, until, finally, it backs out.

So, at this point, I'm thinking that the problem can't be fixed within Windows, at least not by me. So I grab some blank CDs (2), and burn Debian NetInstall onto one of them. I stick the other in her machine's drive/burner and start culling the user dir to make it fit on the disc. I don't manage it (too many ancient photos and Unnamed.docs). I realize I can leave the NTFS partition on the HDD, shrink it, install, copy the user files over into /home/, and then wipe the NTFS and make the ext4 fill the disk. I start doing this when:

Unable to detect network card. Select the driver for your network card:

Sh**. I try to find a list of the hardware in her particular machine, but then various deadlines hit and I say f**k it, I can leave the machine on Vista for now (it's usable).

So, thus ends the story of the totally failed attempt to fix a grandmother's laptop. At some later point I'll go back and get Debian installed properly (with appropriate customized simple desktop).
